email.subject: Case 7731: we have blocked a card payment

body.v: We have blocked a card payment of CHF 389.00 at an online shop. To close the case, we just need to confirm with you that this payment was not yours.
In a few moments you will receive a six-digit code by text message. Simply reply to this email with the code and we will close the case.
Thank you in advance for your help.

hotspots.explain: The domain is swissalpbank-desk.example. The bank's is swissalpbank.example, without "-desk".
No deadline, no threat: a calm, helpful tone that gives you no reason to be suspicious.
The code sent to your phone is there to approve a transaction. A real bank never asks you to send it back or read it out. With this code, the sender can approve their own payment.
The case page is on the same lookalike domain as the sender's address.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone posing as the bank's fraud desk. The address is on swissalpbank-desk.example, not swissalpbank.example.
choices: Your bank's fraud desk, at SwissAlpBank
A colleague trying to do you a favour
Someone with an almost identical address

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Hardly any pressure. The message leans on the authority of a fraud desk and on your wish to help: with a tone this calm, people cooperate gladly.
choices: Authority, and your wish to help

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Send back the code that arrives on your phone. That code approves a transaction or a login, for the sender's benefit.
choices: Click a link and sign in
Pass on the code you get by text

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Do not reply. Call the number on the back of your card, or open the SwissAlpBank app yourself, and ask about case 7731.
choices: Reply with the code to close the case
View the case on the page they give you
Call the number on the back of your card

actions.label: Call the number on the back of your card and ask where the case stands
actions.consequence: The bank has no record of a case 7731. The email was fake.

actions.label: Reply with the code as soon as it arrives
actions.consequence: The sender uses it to approve a payment or sign in as you.

actions.label: View the case on the page they give you
actions.consequence: The page asks for your login details, then your card details. All of it lands with the scammer.

actions.label: Report it as phishing and delete it
actions.consequence: You handed over nothing: no code, no login details.

attacker_reveal: A case number, your first name, a very polite "Marc": nothing urgent, nothing threatening. All I needed were the six digits about to appear on your phone, and no bank will ever ask you for those.
